# Lessons Ledger

<!-- Generated by /lessons assemble — do not edit Record tables directly -->
<!-- Last assembled: 2026-05-30 by Ben Xavier -->

This ledger is a team-shared staging area for lessons captured from task work. The lifecycle is:

```
Task (tagged) → Ledger Staged → Final home via /lessons promote
                                 ├─ skill <name>    (audited by /best-practices)
                                 ├─ claude-md       (loaded every session)
                                 ├─ agent <name>    (agent prompt)
                                 ├─ rule <name>     (.claude/rules/)
                                 ├─ glossary        (glossary.md)
                                 ├─ standard <id>   (standards applicability)
                                 └─ readme <path>   (folder README)
```

**Do not edit this file directly.** Lesson content comes from `<!-- LESSONS LEARNED -->` tags in task docs; record tables come from `## Lesson Records` sections in task docs. Run `/lessons assemble` to regenerate.

**Loading**: Only the `## Staged` section is loaded at session start via `CLAUDE.md`. The `## Promoted` and `## Archived / Superseded` sections are audit trail only.

---

## Staged

Active lessons under reinforcement. When a situation matches one of these, Claude surfaces a prompt before acting; the user picks `apply`, `exception`, `challenged`, or `false-positive`, and `/lessons record` logs the event in the active task.

### [L-ben-002-01] How-to-guide skill behavior must be verified against SKILL.md, not memory
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/002
**Categories**: documentation-accuracy
**Staged**: 2026-04-12

**Principle**: A how-to guide that documents skill behavior drifts the moment a skill version bumps; verify against `SKILL.md`, never from memory or the skeleton's own prose.

**Why**: Three skeleton sections in the project how-to-guide were not just empty but *inaccurate* — `/medtech-docs init` was undercounted (9 questions, not "~8"), `/medtech-docs import-guidance` was an invented action that doesn't exist (real surface is `update-external-references`), and sync-skills was described at the wrong version (skeleton omitted v8.2's `status` and `prune` actions plus the three-way blob-history bucketing). These are the exact sections a new team copies verbatim; wrong action names fail silently and undercounts leave half-scaffolded trees.

**How to apply**: When authoring or refreshing any doc that names a skill action, open that skill's `SKILL.md` Actions section in the same session and reconcile every command string and option against it.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-006-01] Proactively capture strategy and lessons during task work
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/006
**Categories**: process, skill-usage, proactive-capture
**Staged**: 2026-04-12

**Principle**: When working through non-trivial decisions, strategy content and lessons learned must be captured in the active task document with the proper tags (`<!-- STRATEGY CONTENT: domain, topics -->` and `<!-- LESSONS LEARNED: category -->`) **at the moment the decision or lesson emerges**, not as a deferred cleanup pass and never only after the user asks.

**Why**: The user shouldn't ever have to ask "did you capture that as a strategy?" When the question comes, the discipline has already failed — the content was either left in chat or written in discussion form rather than decision form, and decisions about one domain (regulatory) end up filed under another (architecture). Proactive capture must be a reflex.

**How to apply**: Treat the tagged-block insertion as part of making the decision, not a follow-up step. A decision touching two domains gets two STRATEGY blocks. A lesson that lands in the same turn gets a LESSONS LEARNED block in that turn. Codified in `CLAUDE.md` § Working Conventions.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-007-01] Scaffold skills must be topology-aware from day one
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/007
**Categories**: skill-design, scaffold-evolution, topology-awareness
**Staged**: 2026-04-13

**Principle**: A MedTech project-init skill that hardcodes a single-DHF structure cannot be reused across real product ecosystems. Topology — *is this one product or a multi-component ecosystem?* — is as fundamental a decision as regulatory pathway or device class, and the scaffolding must branch on it.

**Why**: The first version of `medtech-docs init` assumed one DHF and one filing. PDLC_DEMO is a multi-component ecosystem (PCA device, on-prem adapter, cloud suite). The mismatch only surfaced during architecture strategy discussion, requiring a migration after content was already in place.

**How to apply**: When authoring or reviewing a scaffold/generator skill, ask *"What are the distinct project shapes this skill must serve?"* before writing the templates. Use an explicit topology parameter instead of hardcoding one shape.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-007-02] Design deliverables live inside the task doc, not as sibling files
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/007
**Categories**: skill-design, scaffold-evolution, topology-awareness
**Staged**: 2026-04-13

**Principle**: When a task spawns a design deliverable — a phase output, a draft spec, a review artifact — it must live **inside the task document** as a new section, not as a separate sibling file. One task, one file.

**Why**: Task 007's Phase P1 design deliverable was first written to a sibling `007-p1-design.md`, leaving the project with two "007" files and fragmenting the task's story. The task skill's SKILL.md had `## Analysis` framed as "optional," which let the default slip to "spin off a sibling." Default should be capture-in-task, always, unless the artifact is explicitly meant to live elsewhere permanently.

**How to apply**: Append new sections to the active task doc for all design / analysis / phase output. If an artifact genuinely belongs elsewhere (a new doc in `docs/`), the task still records what was produced and points to the real location. Codified in `CLAUDE.md` § Working Conventions ("One task, one file").

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-009-01] Strategy domains are shared, not per-DHF
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/009
**Categories**: skill-design
**Staged**: 2026-04-13

**Principle**: Every domain in the `/strategy` registry has `scope: shared`. Strategy is a cross-component story — a multi-DHF platform's regulatory filing strategy describes how all components file together (predicate lineage, PCCP scope, jurisdictional sequence); splitting it fractures the story a reviewer most needs to see whole.

**Why**: Task 007's unified DHF shape correctly pushed design-controls, risk-management, postmarket, and cybersecurity down into `dhfs/<dhf>/`. It incorrectly tried to apply the same logic to *strategy* docs — but strategy is a project-level artifact, not a component-level one. Formal outputs (SDP, SAD, V&V Plan, Risk Mgmt Plan, PMS Plan) still live per-DHF in the dhfs/ tree; only the strategic *briefs* that inform those outputs move up to `docs/project/strategies/`.

**How to apply**: When designing a new shared deliverable, ask "is this the cross-component story?" If yes — one shared doc with per-component callouts inside, not N parallel docs. Per-component specifics still matter; they live as sections in the shared doc, not as separate files.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-012-01] Skill-design lesson: check existing project state before committing to a doc model
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/012
**Categories**: skill-design, task-discipline, project-conventions
**Staged**: 2026-04-14

**Principle**: When a skill action touches a folder whose template prescribes a model, validate against actual project state before designing around the template. Templates can be wrong or stale; the project's lived structure is the better signal.

**Why**: While designing the `update-external-references` action, almost shipped model A (applicability reports) based purely on what the v14 `readme-fda-guidance.md` template said. A 30-second `ls` of `docs/external/standards/` and `docs/external/industry-frameworks/` immediately showed the project was already practicing model B for the other two folders — the v14 template was the outlier, not the norm.

**How to apply**: Before designing a skill action whose output shape is template-prescribed, glob the target folder and its siblings to see what model is already in place; reconcile against the template, and treat divergence as a signal to question the template, not the lived practice.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-012-02] Task-discipline lesson: activate the task before any writes, not after the design phase
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/012
**Categories**: skill-design, task-discipline, project-conventions
**Staged**: 2026-04-14

**Principle**: When starting any non-trivial work session, the first action should be `/task find` or `/task create`, before any tool calls. Don't wait until the gate denies you.

**Why**: Started work without an active task and got blocked by the task-gate hook on the first fresh `Write` call. Earlier `Edit`s in the session had slipped through because the session context already contained those files — but the moment a fresh `Write` was attempted, the gate fired correctly. The gate is doing its job; discipline was off.

**How to apply**: Run `/task find <topic>` as the first action of any session whose intent is to author or modify project content. If a slip happens and the gate denies, follow the exact recovery command printed in the denial — never bypass.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-012-03] Rubric-vs-existing-exclusion lesson: surface conflicts, don't silently defer either way
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/012
**Categories**: skill-design, task-discipline, project-conventions
**Staged**: 2026-04-14

**Principle**: When a Claude action's heuristic disagrees with a captured human decision, **the action's job is to surface the disagreement, not to pick a side.** Both the rubric and the captured decision can be wrong. Only the user has the context to resolve the conflict, and silencing it in either direction loses signal.

**Why**: The `update-external-references` rubric flagged `ihe-profiles.md` as applicable based on PDLC_DEMO's `ehr_integration: true` capability, but the existing `industry-frameworks/README.md` had IHE in its "Evaluated — Not Required" table with the rationale "No imaging workflow integrations in scope." Reverted the import on the wrong assumption that the existing decision should win. User corrected: the prior exclusion was incomplete (considered only IHE's imaging angle, missed the ITI / Pharmacy / Patient Care domains that absolutely apply). Both heuristic and prior decision were partially wrong.

**How to apply**: For any idempotent context-aware action: before applying its heuristic, read the target folder's "Evaluated — Not Required" tables; for any file where the rubric says "applicable" but exclusion contains it, print a CONFLICT block and wait for user resolution before touching either the file or the table. Applies to all idempotent context-aware actions, not just `update-external-references`.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-012-04] Project-conventions lesson: "one task, one file" applies to skill work that touches the project
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/012
**Categories**: skill-design, task-discipline, project-conventions
**Staged**: 2026-04-14

**Principle**: The CLAUDE.md "one task, one file" rule applies even when the work is inside `.claude/skills/` rather than `docs/`. Skill changes that are scoped to a project (designed in conversation with the user, applied to this project's folders) should still be captured in a task doc.

**Why**: Both for the strategy/lessons capture pipeline and so future sessions can find the rationale. The fact that the skill itself lives outside `docs/` doesn't change that.

**How to apply**: If a skill modification is being co-designed with the user on this project, open or activate a task doc and capture the conversation there — even if the deliverable lands under `.claude/skills/`.

### [L-ben-014-01] Skills built inside one project leak that project's taxonomy
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/014
**Categories**: skill-portability
**Staged**: 2026-04-14

**Principle**: A skill authored against a single project's vocabulary will bake that vocabulary into its docs, examples, auto-generated help text, and validator rules — even when the author believes they kept the skill "generic." The leakage is hard to spot until the skill runs against a second project with a different taxonomy.

**Why**: The tracker skill's a/b suffix semantics (Intra-Op / Pre-Op) were documented as "both conventions are valid" in SKILL.md but in practice the validator and help generator assumed the original project's naming throughout. PDLC_DEMO ran fine because the renderer tolerates unknown suffixes, but any reviewer opening the HTML saw stale Intra-Op/Pre-Op terminology in the Phase Scale legend.

**How to apply**: When promoting a project-local skill into a shared registry, budget for a **second-project validation pass** where you actually run it against a different project's taxonomy before calling it generic. Prefer project-defined vocabulary tables over skill-defined defaults — the skill should consume vocabulary, not ship it.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-017-01] AI authoring tools need a bounded blast radius, not a banned blast radius
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/017
**Categories**: ai-tooling, change-control, regulated-workflows
**Staged**: 2026-04-14

**Principle**: The temptation with AI-driven authoring of regulated docs is to wall the AI off from anything signed. That preserves compliance but throws away most of the value. The better pattern is to let the AI work freely in a clearly-bounded "draft" zone and enforce the boundary with tooling (a hook), not policy (a CLAUDE.md rule the model might forget). The freeze point is the boundary; the hook is the enforcement; the in-chat briefing is the handoff to the human.

**Why**: Came out of the change-control design discussion when the user rejected the PR-based enforcement model. The agent is the right place to enforce the rule, because the agent is where the edit is about to happen and where the human context lives. Moving the gate downstream loses the context.

**How to apply**: When designing future skills that touch regulated artifacts (V&V records, risk files, signed protocols), prefer in-chat consent gates over downstream PR / approval gates. Default to Strategy C semantics (git owns drafting, Confluence owns review + sign-off, Windchill owns release) for any future change-control discussion. Reserve PR gates for things that genuinely need a different reviewer than the one in the chat.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-018-01] Bulk conventions sweeps beat per-file editing when N>20 files share a single fix
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/018
**Categories**: audit, skill-registry, convention-sweep
**Staged**: 2026-04-20

**Principle**: When `/best-practices` surfaces N>20 files missing the same structural section, write a small Python pass rather than fan-out. Only fan-out to subagents when the fix requires per-file reasoning.

**Why**: First instinct was to delegate 180 per-file README edits to parallel subagents. A scripted Python pass that inserts a generic Conventions block before `## Changelog` completed the same work in one call, was deterministic, auditable via git diff, and left room to re-author specific folders' conventions later.

**How to apply**: Use this pattern when (a) audit FAILs are distributed across many files but share a single skill-version cause, (b) the fix is mechanical (template insert, stub creation) rather than content-authoring, and (c) severity is Required so deferral pushes the FAIL into the next audit. Do NOT use this pattern when the audit FAIL is a design-decision surface (e.g., "every User Need traces to a measurable acceptance criterion") — those belong in the feature task.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-019-01] Bootstrap headers can poison "since-cursor" logic on first run
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/019
**Categories**: hook-testing, state-file-patterns, retrospective-bootstrap
**Staged**: 2026-04-20

**Principle**: When a skill uses "the most recent dated header" as a since-cursor, the `--retrospective` / "first run" flag must force a full scan regardless of what the file contains. A bootstrap seed is not the same as a real entry, but the parser can't tell them apart structurally.

**Why**: The `medtech-docs` CHANGELOG.md template seeded the file with `## YYYY-MM-DD 00:00 UTC — Project changelog initialized`. The `find_last_dated_header` function correctly found this header and used it as the since-cursor, so `/digest log --retrospective` only saw commits after midnight today — 2 commits instead of the expected 32.

**How to apply**: The fix is explicit: `if retrospective: since = None` takes precedence over auto-discovery. For any new skill where "is the file empty?" gates behavior, also test the "file is pristine bootstrap" case — it's the same shape with different bytes.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-019-02] Project conventions documented in one skill must be honored by every tool that emits cross-artifact text
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/019
**Categories**: conventions, task-references, script-output-formatting
**Staged**: 2026-04-20

**Principle**: When building a new skill that emits text referencing tasks (commit messages, changelog entries, reports, digests), audit the output against every documented project convention at design time, not only at bug-report time. The lessons skill is the canonical registry of these conventions.

**Why**: The task-reference format rule `<person>/<NNN>` is canonical in `lessons/SKILL.md` but was not surfaced in CLAUDE.md or a global memory. When building the digest skill, copied commit subjects verbatim into CHANGELOG.md, which used bare `task NNN:` because that's how the commits were authored. The fix has to live in every tool that *reads* commit subjects and re-emits them.

**How to apply**: Search the lessons skill (and any rule files) before writing output formatters. Also save durable conventions as feedback memories so they surface at session start in subsequent sessions — documentation in a skill file isn't enough if the skill isn't loaded that session.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-020-01] Use repo-local config (`git config --local`) as a lightweight enforcement mechanism
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/020
**Categories**: identity, state-keys, local-config-as-enforcement
**Staged**: 2026-04-20

**Principle**: When a project needs to enforce "on this repo, use X," prefer setting `git config --local` (or the equivalent for whatever tool) at setup time and letting the tool honor it naturally, rather than wrapping the tool with a per-invocation override.

**Why**: Initially built the digest state key on `git config user.email` directly, which meant the key varied based on machine configuration. The user flagged that `project.yml` should drive the right git account — not the other way around. `git config --local` lives in `.git/config` (not committed, per-clone), overrides `--global` for this repo only, and is set once and done. No hooks that run on every session, no bash gymnastics to slug an email.

**How to apply**: For git, `--local` has zero blast radius — other projects on the same box are unaffected. Combine with an idempotent resolver (detect drift, re-align if needed) so the alignment survives clones, git re-init, or accidental user edits.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-021-01] `claude -p` from inside the project is not a pure LLM call
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/021
**Categories**: claude-cli-invocation, context-pollution, hooks-cross-talk
**Staged**: 2026-04-20

**Principle**: Hooks fire during ALL claude sessions by default, including programmatic `-p` sub-invocations. `--disable-slash-commands` does not disable hooks. `--bare` does, but requires an API key. The cheap general-purpose workaround is `cwd=/tmp` + stripped env, which puts the sub-call outside the project tree so hooks don't register.

**Why**: First attempt ran `claude -p` from the project directory. The CLI loaded CLAUDE.md (62k tokens cached per invocation), ran SessionStart hooks, and at Stop time triggered the capture-check hook which complained about missing strategy/lessons content in the active task. The LLM — asked to return JSON summaries — instead responded to the hook's blocking message and actually wrote to the task file.

**How to apply**: When invoking `claude -p` as a sub-process for pure LLM work, change cwd to `/tmp` and strip the project env to avoid hooks + CLAUDE.md context. Conversely, if the sub-call WANTS the project context (asking Claude to review current state), invoke from the project dir normally. The two modes are intentionally different.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-030-01] Sync hygiene — symlinks need explicit handling; allowlists drift silently
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/030
**Categories**: sync, registry-hygiene, hooks
**Staged**: 2026-04-27

**Principle**: Two recurring failure modes in `/sync-skills pull`: (1) symlinks in the registry require explicit handling because the pull-file primitive does a literal `cp` that either copies the symlink target string or follows the link; (2) `approved_skills` allowlists drift silently whenever new skills appear upstream and need a `project.yml` reconciliation after every pull.

**Why**: After a pull, restoring `agents/project-secops.md` required deleting the copied content file and creating the symlink manually. Sync's check-script also misreports symlinked files as perpetually UPSTREAM_NEWER. Separately, each pull that introduces new skills requires a project.yml diff against `security.approved_skills` to keep the audit clean — a `/best-practices` check enforces this; running it after every sync catches the drift earlier.

**How to apply**: After any `/sync-skills pull`: (1) check the install of any agents that pull as new files vs. expected symlinks, fix locally; (2) immediately edit `project.yml` `security.approved_skills` to add any new skills before the next session-start audit.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-034-01] Plan-first when scoping a meta-analysis of project history
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/034
**Categories**: process-discipline
**Staged**: 2026-04-27

**Principle**: For any "summarize a year of work" ask — always do the index-level read + category lock first, in the task doc, with example seeds; never go straight to long-form writing.

**Why**: When asked for a build-process addendum, the temptation was to start pulling examples and writing prose. The right move was the wide-scan-then-categorize approach: read index files / CHANGELOGs / sync-logs first, lock 10 candidate categories with seed task IDs, state the tentative thesis, *then* propose phased deep dives. This both produces a better artifact and gives the user a clean review surface — they can redirect categories before any expensive content is written.

**How to apply**: For a corpus of >20 task docs or any cross-history synthesis, gate the writing phase behind a categorization + seed-id step in the task doc. Diving into examples without a category map produces a list, not a synthesis.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-034-02] Lead commercial pitches with audit-trail, not feature comparison
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/034
**Categories**: commercial-positioning
**Staged**: 2026-04-27

**Principle**: When a prospect says "we already use Copilot/Cursor/Gemini, we're already agentic," the right move is **not** to argue about agents — it's to ask: *"can your auditor open your repo today and see every guardrail enforced?"* Copilot users say no. The pivot is from "do you use AI?" (everyone does) to "is your AI usage auditable, reusable, and project-shape-bonded?" (almost no one's is).

**Why**: Reframes the conversation from feature-comparison (Copilot vs. Claude) to system-property comparison (auditable agentic shape vs. ad-hoc usage). Buyers in regulated industries respond to the second framing because it's the one their compliance org will ask about.

**How to apply**: In GTM conversations, lead with audit-trail and project-shape, not model brand or productivity %.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-038-01] `frontend-slides` skill is the right default for executive deck builds
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/038
**Categories**: tooling
**Staged**: 2026-04-29

**Principle**: When user asks for "a deck" — invoke `/frontend-slides`, pre-pick the preset based on audience mood (board pitch → Bold Signal; technical seminar → Swiss Modern; tutorial → Notebook Tabs), and inline the full viewport-base.css.

**Why**: First use of this skill on this project showed the viewport-base.css mandatory contents must be inlined in full into the deck `<style>` block (non-negotiable per the skill's Phase 3 requirements). The skill also enforces clamp() for all type/spacing — this is what makes the deck render correctly at 1280×720 (typical projector) and 1920×1080 (laptop) without rework.

**How to apply**: Use STYLE_PRESETS.md's mood mapping to skip the discovery phase. Inline viewport-base.css verbatim. Trust clamp() for sizing.

### [L-ben-039-01] Commit early and often when the work lives outside HEAD
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/039
**Categories**: tooling, operations
**Staged**: 2026-04-30

**Principle**: When a skill or any non-trivial code artifact is being authored in `.claude/skills/<new-skill>/`, stage and commit after every working iteration — minimum once per "this output looks right in the browser" milestone.

**Why**: On 2026-05-01 the entire `.claude/skills/md-deck/` directory was deleted between iterations of an extended v0.2 rebuild — surgically, while the rest of `.claude/` was rolled back in unstaged form (recoverable from HEAD). md-deck specifically was unrecoverable from git because no commit had ever staged it. ~2000 lines of working Python plus a session of design decisions had to be reconstructed from the conversation transcript. WSL's ext4 has no recycle bin for in-WSL deletes; git is the only durable safety net.

**How to apply**: Use a WIP branch if needed, or atomic `git add -p` with a one-line message; do not let an evening's work sit untracked. The cost of a noisy commit history is trivial compared to the cost of reconstructing from a transcript.

### [L-ben-039-02] Component extraction is the load-bearing investment for deck authoring
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/039
**Categories**: tooling, design-systems
**Staged**: 2026-04-30

**Principle**: The bug class in slide authoring (geometry math, renumbering, positioning) mostly disappears for the next deck once you have a named, parameterized component library — not by fixing the bugs one at a time.

**Why**: Authoring time on ben/038 was ~80% on geometry math and renumbering, ~20% on actual content decisions. Once a component is named and parameterized (e.g., `event-timeline` knows how to position above/below markers correctly), the bug class disappears for the next deck.

**How to apply**: When building skill-driven slide tooling, prioritize the component library over individual feature work — the component layer is the multiplier for everything downstream.

### [L-ben-041-01] Regex SAST self-matches its own rule strings — expected, don't engineer around it
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/041
**Categories**: secops, static-analysis
**Staged**: 2026-05-01

**Principle**: Any scanner that stores rules as Python data and lives inside the tree it audits will detect itself. The trade-off is between (a) keeping rules readable and centralized vs. (b) silencing self-matches at the cost of either putting the rule data in a separate file or special-casing the scanner's own path.

**Why**: When adding new rules to `audit_artifacts.py`, accept that the rule definitions themselves may match. Worth knowing for any future SAST-style skills before someone builds an over-clever suppression mechanism.

**How to apply**: Document expected self-matches inline in the Findings table rather than building suppression machinery for them. If a future rule pattern is too noisy when applied to its own definition, move that rule's pattern to a sidecar file rather than trying to teach the scanner to skip its own rule block.

### [L-ben-042-01] Shared-layer pattern as a model for future skill pairs
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/042
**Categories**: skill-composition
**Staged**: 2026-05-01

**Principle**: When two skills overlap at infrastructure (CSS, scripts, registries) but diverge at the user-facing contract (interactive wizard vs. deterministic CLI), the right shape is **one canonical owner + a path-aware consumer**, not a merge.

**Why**: Pick the skill with the better-structured infrastructure as canonical owner. Move shared assets into a clearly-named subdirectory. The consumer skill resolves assets path-aware with a fallback. Both SKILL.md files declare the relationship explicitly: a "Relationship to <other>" or "Used by <other>" section with a file-ownership table. A "Non-goals" section in the consumer skill prevents future scope creep.

**How to apply**: When considering merging two skills with overlapping infrastructure, evaluate whether the user-facing contracts actually diverge — if yes, keep them separate with the canonical-owner + consumer pattern. This split survived a green build with zero regressions and unblocks multi-preset support without further architecture work.

### [L-ben-044-01] Aggregation rules must be structural, not semantic
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/044
**Categories**: tracker-skill, classifier-design
**Staged**: 2026-05-05

**Principle**: When a classifier needs an aggregation behavior for a content type (e.g., "Benefit-Risk Analyses should aggregate"), code the *structural pattern* the type exhibits (N numbered files matching `PREFIX-NNNN` plus optional aggregator summary doc, all single-role), not a per-type special case. The rule lives in the skill once; future content types inherit aggregation for free.

**Why**: User explicitly named this constraint: "I don't want to have to be explicit and bloat the skills per type, we need language that allows the skills/agent to make that assessment." The anti-pattern is the heuristic ever needing to grep for a content-type name.

**How to apply**: When adding a classifier behavior to a skill, ask "what structural shape am I really keying off of?" If you find yourself writing `if content_type == "benefit-risk":`, restate the rule in terms of the file-naming pattern instead.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-044-02] `project.yml dhfs[].path` is project-root-relative, not leaf-only
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/044
**Categories**: tracker-skill, configuration
**Staged**: 2026-05-05

**Principle**: The tracker generator and `/tracker assess` both do literal path resolution (`project_root / dhf.path`); there is no `docs/project/dhfs/` prefix logic anywhere. Project.yml `dhfs[].path` must carry the full project-root-relative path.

**Why**: The original project.yml comment read "folder name under docs/project/dhfs/ (or nested path)" — misleading, and led to silent zero-row generator output across the tracker. Future projects scaffolded from a template will inherit whatever `path` convention they're given; getting it wrong produces empty tracker output with no clear error.

**How to apply**: When scaffolding a new project, write full `docs/project/dhfs/<leaf>` paths into every `dhfs[].path` entry from day one. When debugging an empty tracker, check this first.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-044-03] Tracker milestone IDs are matched against a hardcoded prefix map
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/044
**Categories**: tracker-skill, milestone-catalog
**Staged**: 2026-05-05

**Principle**: `regulatory.yml` milestone IDs are matched against a hardcoded `ms_prefix_map` in `generate.py`: `qsub-release` → Q, `pccp-release` → no-prefix (baseline), `lmr1-release` → L1, `lmr2-release` → L2. Using milestone IDs that aren't in this map produces rows with empty milestone prefix (so all rows collide at PC1, PC2…).

**Why**: Projects that need a different filing strategy (e.g., De Novo, PMA, IDE-then-PMA) need to either (a) reuse these IDs as conceptual placeholders, or (b) extend the prefix map in `generate.py`.

**How to apply**: When authoring `regulatory.yml` for a non-510(k) pathway, reuse the canonical four IDs as placeholders OR open a tracker-skill task to extend the prefix map before authoring.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-044-04] Hardcoded path walks silently drop evidence; taxonomy is the antidote
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/044
**Categories**: tracker-skill, evidence-discovery
**Staged**: 2026-05-05

**Principle**: Hardcoded path walks (e.g., `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_DHF_ROLE_MAP` in tracker's `generate.py`) silently drop evidence not in the canonical layout AND collapse multi-file folders to one alphabetically-sorted winner. The brittleness is invisible — the generator just produces fewer rows. Taxonomy + reconcile + `pending:` block are the antidote: discovery is explicit, ambiguities surface as conflicts the user resolves, and re-scans can detect drift over time.

**Why**: Discovered while investigating why the original 118-row tracker collapsed to a 44-row generator candidate. The other 74 rows weren't lost data — they were evidence the hardcoded walk couldn't see.

**How to apply**: Before adding new evidence to a project, check whether the discovery mechanism (taxonomy or hardcoded walk) will actually see it. If hardcoded, either (a) add the file to a canonical-named location, or (b) advocate for taxonomy adoption in the relevant skill.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-044-05] Check sister projects before redesigning skills
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/044
**Categories**: tracker-skill, sister-project-compat
**Staged**: 2026-05-05

**Principle**: Before redesigning a skill or schema, check whether sister projects in the same registry have already converged on a solution. Naming collisions, vocabulary mismatches, and multi-DHF assumptions in your design can silently corrupt their data.

**Why**: Arthrex (sister project at `../../projects/arthrex/pccp/`) was significantly ahead on the tracker taxonomy problem space — already had a working v0.2 taxonomy (155 lines, shared across 3 external-mode item DHFs) plus a developed `tracker.status_vocabulary` block implementing the AI-vs-User-Status dual model PDLC_DEMO was about to design. Three things would have broken if PDLC_DEMO's redesign had proceeded blind: `unmapped:` naming collision, status vocabulary conflict, and multi-DHF shared-taxonomy assumption mismatch.

**How to apply**: Before drafting a schema change to any registry-shared skill, search sister projects for the same concept. Adopt their vocabulary if they've already shipped; only diverge with explicit reason.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-045-01] Sync-skill pulls that change path constants require a coordinated producer-side rebuild
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/045
**Categories**: skill-pulls
**Staged**: 2026-05-05

**Principle**: Pulls that rename consumer-side path constants (e.g., where a loader looks for sidecars) require a coordinated **producer-side rebuild** as a post-update migration step. On-disk sidecar files don't move automatically; stale `trace-matrix.yml` `output_dir` overrides further mask the rename — even pressing the in-app Build button writes to the old path.

**Why**: Discovered after a sync renamed the trace-matrix sidecar contract from `docs/project/dhfs/<leaf>/design-controls/trace-matrix/trace-matrix.json` → `docs/project/console/<leaf>/console_trace_matrix.json` symmetrically in producer + consumer code, but no rebuild was run and `trace-matrix.yml` still pinned the OLD `output_dir`. The view broke silently.

**How to apply**: Add a check to `/sync-skills pull` post-update flow: after pulling skills, scan project for `trace-matrix.yml` (and analogous skill config files) for path overrides that no longer match the skill's default; surface as drift. Until that's implemented, post-pull migration checklists must include "regenerate any sidecars whose output paths moved."

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-047-01] `render.py::rewrite_url()` double-prefixes project-root-relative paths
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/047
**Categories**: skill-render
**Staged**: 2026-05-11

**Principle**: The tracker `render.py::rewrite_url()` resolves relative links against `src_dir` (the canonical markdown's directory) rather than the project root, so any `[label](docs/project/...)` written into a tracker md outside `docs/project/submissions/` gets double-prefixed in the dashboard.

**Why**: Workaround: write paths pre-rewritten as `[label](/documents#path=<project-relative>)` — the leading `/` short-circuits the rewriter via `url.startswith('/')` at line 132. Permanent fix is a render.py change to detect project-root-relative paths (any path starting with `docs/` resolves from `project_dir`, not `src_dir`).

**How to apply**: When authoring tracker overlays, use the `/documents#path=` form, not bare project-relative paths. Push the render.py fix upstream when the next batch of tracker improvements ships.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-047-02] Tracker generator picks alphabetically-first file; templates win against real content
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/047
**Categories**: skill-generator
**Staged**: 2026-05-11

**Principle**: `generate.py::discover_system_dhf_evidence()` picks the alphabetically-first non-README `.md` as the canonical row Path. `GL-TMP-*` template scaffolds win against real authored content (`design-inputs.md`, `user-needs-register.md`, etc.) by alphabetical order.

**Why**: Workaround: per-row `path:` override in the overlay. Permanent fix: rank files by classifier (real > SOP > template) before picking the canonical.

**How to apply**: When authoring real content into a DHF folder that also contains GL-TMP templates, either delete the template files or add the row to the tracker overlay with an explicit `path:` override. Same upstream batch as the `rewrite_url` fix.

### [L-ben-049-01] Don't trust task-doc strategy blocks about skill internals without re-reading the skill
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/049
**Categories**: skill-internals
**Staged**: 2026-05-12

**Principle**: Prior-conversation memory of skill behavior is not authoritative; the skill code is. Even when a prior session left a strategy block claiming a fact, re-verify by reading the actual file before basing a plan on it.

**Why**: The task creation strategy block said the default software parser mirrors the DI tokenizer. Read of `parsers/defaults/software.py` showed it's a no-op `return ParserResult()`. This is exactly what the `read-skill-before-planning` rule warns about.

**How to apply**: For any plan that depends on a skill's internal behavior, Read the relevant file (`parsers/`, `scripts/`, `SKILL.md`) before committing to the plan — even if a prior task doc tells you what it does.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-049-02] Adding a SW layer can break the V&V layer in DHFs that relied on DI-derived VER nodes
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/049
**Categories**: tooling
**Staged**: 2026-05-12

**Principle**: When SW is present, `graph.py` filters V&V to "tests that verify SW reqs," requiring `vnv.traces_forward_ids` to point at SW. Default DI-derived VER nodes carry only `verifies_di_ids`, not `traces_forward_ids→SW`, so they're filter-dropped — and the DI→VER edges that referenced them become `broken_refs`.

**Why**: Confirmed on pca-device (4 broken refs), connectivity-adapter (21), cloud-suite (22). The DI→SW chain works correctly either way; the V&V layer is the casualty.

**How to apply**: Before adding a SW layer to a DHF that has VER references in its DI doc, plan for either (a) a skill enhancement to enrich VER nodes with SW-trace info, or (b) authoring a dedicated V&V protocol doc with explicit SW traces.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-049-03] `scripts/analyze.py` does not enumerate the `software` layer
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/049
**Categories**: tooling
**Staged**: 2026-05-12

**Principle**: The trace-matrix analyze script's `LAYER_KEYS` constant omits `software`. So `/trace-matrix analyze` and `/trace-matrix init` (which depends on analyze) silently skip the SW layer; you can't use `analyze` to drive SW-adapter generation.

**Why**: `scripts/build.py` handles software correctly. The bug is one line in analyze (add `"software"` to `LAYER_KEYS`).

**How to apply**: Workaround: read the source doc shape, write the project adapter directly by hand, then run `build` to verify. Schedule the one-line fix upstream.

### [L-ben-049-04] `/trace-matrix init` is one-shot, not a re-detector
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/049
**Categories**: tooling
**Staged**: 2026-05-12

**Principle**: SKILL.md step 2 says init writes `trace-matrix.yml` only "if `trace-matrix.yml` does not exist." If the yml already exists pointing at the wrong source paths (e.g., conventional `user-needs.md` when the DHF has `user-needs-register.md`), init won't re-detect — it'll silently keep stale paths.

**Why**: Confirmed on connectivity-adapter + cloud-suite.

**How to apply**: Hand-edit `trace-matrix.yml` when a DHF's actual source filenames diverge from the convention, or delete the yml and re-init (heavyweight).

### [L-ben-049-05] Empty `missing_reason: no_items_parsed` doesn't always mean "parser broken"
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/049
**Categories**: tooling
**Staged**: 2026-05-12

**Principle**: When a trace-matrix layer reports `no_items_parsed`, check (a) does the source path exist? (b) is the file populated, not a stub? Don't assume parser bug.

**Why**: Both connectivity-adapter and cloud-suite returned this verdict pre-fix; on inspection the source files were placeholder stubs containing only `{{Populate per the parent QMS template — e.g., UN/DI rows with IDs, criteria, traceability}}`. Parser was fine — the source had no items. The trace-matrix.yml path was *also* wrong (pointing at `user-needs.md` when only `user-needs-register.md` existed). Both gaps had to be fixed.

**How to apply**: For any "no items parsed" diagnostic, audit (1) trace-matrix.yml source path matches a file that exists, (2) the file isn't a `{{...}}` stub, before suspecting the parser.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-051-01] Silent-drop failure modes hide real bugs and blunt the diagnostic surface
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/051
**Categories**: skill-resilience, debuggability
**Staged**: 2026-05-12

**Principle**: For resolver/diagnostic code: **never drop information at a branch.** If a function gathers candidates that the happy path doesn't consume, the unhappy path must still surface them — and the gap/error message must accurately name the actual cause (multi-match-no-winner ≠ no-match).

**Why**: The dhf-manifest discovery-index resolver was silently dropping multi-match-no-winner cases into a misleading "no file matched any pattern" gap reason — both lying about the cause AND throwing away the candidate list that would have made the gap actionable. The cost was invisible until a downstream task surfaced it via a project-side override that papered over the symptom.

**How to apply**: When designing any resolver / classifier / discovery layer, audit every branch that returns "empty" / "no-match" / "not-found" and confirm the message accurately distinguishes cause from absence-of-evidence. Applies to `/trace-matrix` adapters, `/tracker` evidence-walks, `/best-practices` audit findings.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-053-01] Iframes are the right answer for thumbnailing third-party HTML
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/053
**Categories**: ui-design
**Staged**: 2026-05-13

**Principle**: Three small UX patterns from the slide-curation UI worth keeping: **(a)** iframes are the right answer for thumbnailing third-party HTML — they isolate CSS, give a clean viewport for `vw`/`vh` to resolve against, and `pointer-events: none` lets parent drag/click bubble up; transform-scale tricks fight the source's viewport-relative units. **(b)** Random-access position-input beats sequential ▲/▼ once N > ~10. **(c)** Auto-detect drag-direction from tile vs viewport size — same JS handler works for grid and stacked layouts without a mode flag.

**Why**: Verified in Chrome on a 126-slide curation grid: 4 columns × ~11 rows; typed "1" into slide-42's position-input → slide jumped to position 1, all positions cascaded correctly.

**How to apply**: When thumbnailing third-party HTML in a curation tool, reach for iframes before transform-scale. When N>10 in a reorder UI, add a position-input alongside the up/down buttons.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-053-02] Two-pass workflow pattern: split selection from ordering when candidate pool > ~30
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/053
**Categories**: ui-design
**Staged**: 2026-05-13

**Principle**: When a curation tool combines selection + ordering and the candidate pool is large (>~30 items), the cognitive load of doing both at once is the bug. Split into focused passes — each pass is one decision per slide. The price is round-trip state semantics (what survives Pass A → B → A?), but a single `_build_id` + a "preserve prior order on export" rule covers it.

**Why**: User feedback after seeing the 126-slide candidate: judging keep/remove + reordering simultaneously was too much. Splitting into Pass 1 (SELECT, source order, KEEP/REMOVE only) and Pass 2 (REORDER, only kept slides) made the workflow tractable.

**How to apply**: For any future curation tool with N>30 candidate items, default to two-pass UX with explicit round-trip rules. Use a `_build_id` fingerprint so stale state across rebuilds is detected.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-053-03] When you strip the runtime that drives a state machine, pin the state CSS class at build time
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/053
**Categories**: build-debug
**Staged**: 2026-05-13

**Principle**: First candidate render of the composite deck showed empty slides because source decks gated `.reveal` content on `.slide.visible <thing>` (set by IntersectionObserver in their stripped inline JS). Fix wasn't to add the JS back (3-deck script collisions), it was a one-line `_ensure_visible()` that stamps `visible` into every section's class list at build time — lets the deck's own animation-end CSS rules win.

**Why**: When you strip the runtime that drives a state machine, find the state CSS class and pin it at build time.

**How to apply**: When merging multiple HTML decks into one and one of them stops rendering, audit whether the source deck has a runtime that toggles a class. If so, stamp the class at build time rather than re-importing the runtime.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-056-01] A binary check on a tri-state signal manufactures false negatives
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/056
**Categories**: skill-resilience, debuggability
**Staged**: 2026-05-13

**Principle**: For check/assertion code: if the underlying signal has an "unknown" state, the check must have a SKIP state — never collapse unknown into the negative outcome.

**Why**: `gh api /user` returns 2FA status as `true` / `false` / `null`, where `null` means "this token can't see it" — a fundamentally different thing from `false`. The `// false` jq fallback erased that distinction, turning "undeterminable" into "Critical FAIL." Same failure shape as the dhf-manifest multi-match-no-winner bug (ben/051): dropping information at a branch.

**How to apply**: When writing any check that reads from an external API or config that can return null/missing, model the result as a three-state (PASS / FAIL / SKIP), not a boolean. Document the SKIP cases inline.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-059-01] Skill-shipped rules go under `skills/<name>/rules/`, never a registry-root `rules/` namespace
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/059
**Categories**: skill-architecture
**Staged**: 2026-05-15

**Principle**: `/sync-skills` scans only `skills/` and `agents/`. Agents get a symlink-vs-content false positive (ben/029) because they have a registry-root `agents/` namespace *and* are symlink-installed into `.claude/agents/` — a symlink lands inside a scanned namespace. Keeping a rule's canonical source inside the owning skill means sync-skills only ever diffs the real file; the `.claude/rules/` symlink is invisible to it.

**Why**: Avoids reproducing the ben/029 false positive for a whole new artifact class.

**How to apply**: Any future skill-shipped, symlink-installed artifact should keep its canonical source inside the skill dir, not at a new registry-root namespace.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._

### [L-ben-066-01] Windows `core.symlinks=false` is a silent corruption vector for any cross-OS shared repo with git-tracked symlinks
**Status**: staged
**Origin**: ben/066
**Categories**: tooling, cross-platform
**Staged**: 2026-05-30

**Principle**: Git on Windows defaults to storing symlinks as plain text files containing the target path string, but **keeps the index mode at 120000**. Any tool that (a) reads the file as text and (b) writes new content to that path will commit the new content under the preserved 120000 mode — producing a "symlink" whose target string is arbitrary bytes. Receiving systems (Linux/macOS) then refuse to check it out.

**Why**: The bug is invisible on the Windows side (file looks fine, commit succeeds, push succeeds) and only surfaces downstream.

**How to apply**: Tools operating on shared repos with symlinks must precheck `core.symlinks` + scan for tracked 120000 entries and refuse / warn when both conditions hold. Sync-skills and agent-installers are the highest-risk consumers.

**Records** (0 applied, 0 exception, 0 challenged, 0 false-positive): _no records yet._
